findings.title: Delete (and Pause) disappear from the alert list menu even though permissions allow them
findings.body: The Delete item is rendered only when `canDelete && rulerRule`. The list view no longer passes `rulerRule` (GrafanaRuleListItem renders RuleActionsButtons with only `promRule`), so the item is never shown, even though `canDelete` now correctly comes from the promRule-based ability. Users with AlertingRuleDelete lose Delete from the list, which the previous GrafanaRuleLoader path offered. The same gating applies to Pause at line 123 (`MenuItemPauseRule rule={rulerRule}` requires a ruler rule), so Pause is also unreachable while `canPause` is true. Either wire delete/pause to the identifier-based path or stop computing these abilities for the list view; as written, the abilities and the rendered menu disagree.

findings.title: Silence item is shown in the list view but clicking it does nothing
findings.body: `canSilence` is now true in the list view via the promRule-based ability, so the 'Silence notifications' item renders and calls `handleSilence`. That handler sets `showSilenceDrawer` in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, but the drawer is only mounted when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true (see RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx line 104). In the list view `rule` is undefined, so the drawer never renders and the click is a silent no-op. Either migrate SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer to accept the Grafana prom rule, or hide the item when no ruler rule is present.

findings.title: Silence drawer is gated on the ruler rule, which is always undefined in the list view
findings.body: The condition `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer` requires the ruler DTO. The list view intentionally passes only `promRule`, so `rule` is undefined and the drawer (which also takes `rulerRule`) can never open. Combined with the new silence ability in AlertRuleMenu, this exposes a control that visibly does nothing.

findings.title: Federated-group check was dropped, so federated rules become editable through useAllAlertRuleAbilities
findings.body: Previously useAllAlertRuleAbilities computed `isFederated` from `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. The refactor routes that hook through useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifier), which has no access to the group's `source_tenants`, and hard-codes `const isFederated = false` (TODO). useAllAlertRuleAbilities is still exported and used by callers (it is only marked deprecated), so for federated rule groups Update/Delete/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently are now treated as mutable whenever the user has permission. This is a regression of existing behavior for those callers. The federation information should be passed through the new signature rather than removed.

findings.title: Test asserts the 4-item list menu, locking in the missing Delete/Pause actions, and does not exercise the actions
findings.body: The test grants AlertingRuleDelete and expects exactly four menu items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export), so it codifies the omission of Delete (and Pause) in the list view. The comment at line 191 says 'all 4 menu actions should be available' while the user has delete permission, which is misleading. No test verifies that clicking Silence opens the drawer, that Delete is reachable, or that Pause works from the list. The unused `ui.menuItems.delete` helper suggests the delete case was meant to be tested. Tests should reflect the intended list-view action set and cover the click behavior.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered in a mapped list without a key
findings.body: The grafana branch previously passed `key={key}` (the computed rule key). The refactor to `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} ... />` drops the key while the other branches still use it. React will warn about missing keys and fall back to index identity, and component-local state (silence drawer, clone redirect in RuleActionsButtons) is then keyed by position rather than by rule. Pass `key={key}` to restore consistent identity.

findings.title: Link to the rule view no longer carries returnTo
findings.body: The removed GrafanaRuleLoader built the view href with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new component builds `/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view` without returnTo, so rule-view navigation back to the list (which relies on returnTo, e.g. via useReturnToPrevious) is lost. This is an unmentioned behavior change; restore the returnTo parameter or document its removal.

findings.title: Doc comment still says the loader reads from the Ruler endpoint
findings.body: The doc comment says 'Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints', but after this change the component only queries the Prometheus endpoint (the ruler query was removed). Line 19 in the `expectedRulesCount` prop docs similarly refers to the ruler response, which is no longer consulted. Update the comments to match the implementation.

findings.title: Every list row now computes both ruler and Grafana ability sets, twice
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu calls useRulerRuleAbilities (with rulerRule undefined in the list view) and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, and RuleActionsButtons.V2 separately calls useRulerRuleAbility and useGrafanaPromRuleAbility. Each of these runs the full useAll*RuleAbilities computation, including folder lookups and the silence-status query, so each rule row runs the ability logic about four times, even though the ruler-based results are always neutral in the list view. The list page's own comment notes this hook is already called for ~80 rules, so the duplication scales poorly. Compute the abilities once per row or skip the ruler path when rulerRule is absent.

findings.title: Immutability of list-view rules now depends on a provenance field the Prometheus endpoint must return
findings.body: `provenance` was added to GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase, and isProvisionedPromRule uses it to disable Update/Delete/Pause for provisioned rules in the list view (previously read from the ruler). If the Prometheus-compatible groups endpoint does not populate `provenance`, provisioned rules will appear editable in the list and editing them will fail server-side. This PR does not include the backend change, so the dependency should be confirmed and called out.
